correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID 9989
correspondence.finding: The creek trends south and southeast through the Fort Polk/Vernon wooded uplands, receives the mapped Birds Creek connection, continues through the LA 399 and LA 112 corridor and bends southeast toward the LA 377/LA 26 area. It receives Sixmile Creek and then Tenmile Creek from the eastern side, and Bundick Creek from the west farther downstream. It remains the Whisky Chitto corridor until joining the separate Calcasieu River branch just north of US 190 west of Kinder. The selected continuation then follows Calcasieu River southwest and south through its broad wooded floodplain, with Barnes Creek and the lower bayou connections, to the River Road/Goss vicinity.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at generalized corridor scale
correspondence.headward_setting: The selected opening lies on the mapped upper Whisky Chitto Creek corridor in the Vernon Parish/Fort Polk setting. The map shows the stream continuing headward beyond the selected opening, so that opening is not asserted to be the official river source.
correspondence.junctions_and_waterbodies: The original upper and middle maps distinguish the lateral Bundick Lake–Bundick Creek system from the selected route: the selection does not traverse Bundick Lake. No large intervening on-route reservoir is depicted. The lower Calcasieu floodplain is mapped with many sloughs, ponds, meanders and wetland symbols; not every side channel is named here.
correspondence.prose_scope: LDEQ supplies the bounded Fort Polk-to-Calcasieu tributary relationship and general basin setting; cartography establishes selected-route correspondence and junction placement.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID 9990
correspondence.finding: The selected segment continues along the mapped Calcasieu River meanders between the Goss/River Road area and Moss Bluff, then turns south past the US 171 crossing toward the upper Lake Charles estuary. Floodplain wetlands and adjoining abandoned/meandering channels remain distinct from the selected generalized river corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at generalized corridor scale
correspondence.junctions_and_waterbodies: The maps continuously connect this segment with FID 9989 upstream and FID 9991 downstream; there is no intervening lake or source-coverage break. West Fork Calcasieu River approaches the downstream estuarine reach from the west.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID 9991
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation is the Calcasieu River through the West Fork Calcasieu River junction and the broad meandering reach north of I-10. It follows the connected western Lake Charles passage and then the river/navigation-channel corridor beside the Clooney Island/Coon Island complex, Prien Lake and Moss Lake. Farther south it continues into the long, nearly north–south Calcasieu Ship Channel along the western side of the Calcasieu Lake complex, through the Long Point/West Cove and lower Calcasieu Pass setting, to the open Gulf coast.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at generalized corridor scale
correspondence.junctions_and_waterbodies: The original lower map shows the West Fork connection, Lake Charles, Prien Lake, Moss Lake, the Calcasieu Lock/Intracoastal Waterway connection east of the selected channel, Calcasieu Lake and West Cove, and the East Fork/West Fork Calcasieu Pass connections beside the selected ship channel. These are connected settings, not an assertion that the selected line crosses the center of every named lake or follows every natural side loop. No reservoir is inferred from these estuarine lakes.
correspondence.actual_terminal: Open Gulf coast at the Calcasieu Pass/Calcasieu Ship Channel entrance south of Cameron. Calcasieu Lake is an intervening connected estuarine waterbody, not the terminal. The retained model sea-terminal classification is compatible at this generalized scale; the exact shore/mouth vertex is not assessed.
correspondence.prose_scope: LDEQ supports the general Calcasieu-to-Gulf terminal relationship; the original lower cartography independently depicts the selected ship-channel/coastal connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern mountain-foot headward approach
correspondence.finding: The southeastern selected opening lies in the mountain-foot and bajada setting around Cerro El Gringo, Cerro Las Vírgenes and Cerro El Cabrero. The Mazapil relief original depicts small drainage there and a westward approach toward the Salitrillo corridor; the statewide original adds the local mountain, settlement and intermittent-channel context. No single hydronym is assigned to this entire opening or its westward turn.
correspondence.correspondence: Component geography supported; full route remains pending at the lower connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Salitrillo–El Paisanito upper and middle corridor
correspondence.finding: The Mazapil relief map shows the northwest-trending Arroyo Salitrillo valley, the Tanque El Ranchito setting, and the continuation labeled El Paisanito toward the wider lowland. Its independently drawn Los Hacheros approach joins from the east; the western Arroyo Seco system and Tanque La Calavera are separate branches or nearby features, not alternate names for every selected segment. The modern state map distinguishes San Benito (El Salitrillo), Majoma, the La Fortuna / Noria del Junco area, and several shortened intermittent streams. These sources establish ordinary corridor correspondence, not permanent water continuity or exact name-transition vertices.
correspondence.correspondence: Component geography supported; full route remains pending at the lower connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Las Playas lower middle corridor and junctions
correspondence.finding: The Mazapil relief original maps the selected northwest passage along the Las Playas corridor west of the elongated mountain belt. It separately shows the Santa Rosa and Tanquecillos approaches from the eastern hills before the lowland reaches the Durango boundary. The state sheet distinguishes the Gruñidora flood-prone flats, Las Playas, the Nuevo Mercurio / San Marcos setting, Estación Camacho and the farther-north plain. This does not establish that every small tank or nearby flood polygon is crossed by the selected channel.
correspondence.correspondence: Component geography supported; full route remains pending at the lower connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Bajío El Barreal / Cuenca El Pajonal lower connector
correspondence.finding: The final northwest-to-west selected approach traverses the broad flat country east of Laguna La Mancha. San Juan de Guadalupe's municipal original maps the lake and eastern plain but does not provide a continuous eastern feeder for this approach. The more detailed Estación Symon G13-D68 original labels Bajío El Barreal, Llanos El Barreal and Cuenca El Pajonal and depicts isolated intermittent channels, numerous small tanks and the lake. It does not establish the selected through-going surface connector across that plain. Roads, tracks, geological contacts, a common plain and modeled connectivity are not used as substitute channel evidence.
correspondence.correspondence: material_connector_unresolved

correspondence.component_scope: Actual Laguna La Mancha terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The actual selected endpoint setting is the mapped La Mancha waterbody beside San Antonio de la Laguna, northeast of San Juan de Guadalupe. INEGI's municipal hydrography table classifies La Mancha as intermittent; the state map uses intermittent-waterbody symbology. The original 1:50,000 SGM sheet prints Laguna La Mancha and shows the lake with small tanks along its southern side, distinct from surrounding ephemeral stream ends. The SGM inventory prose describes lacustrine silts, clays and fine sands there. This establishes the endpoint's geographic setting, without proving a continuous hydrologic link from all upstream selected components.
correspondence.correspondence: Component geography supported; full route remains pending at the lower connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Extreme headward upland feeder and its junction with the Yaminué canyon drainage
correspondence.finding: The southern selected setting is on the Somuncurá upland northwest of Puesto Buñuelo. The readable detailed original depicts an unnamed dashed/intermittent southeast feeder running northwest on the southwest side of Cerro León, passing south of Laguna Mata Niyeu and joining the drainage in Cañadón de Yaminué. A separate southerly headwater arm approaches from the Cerro La Chara area. This is the selected southeast approach, not the separate southerly arm or a traversal of Laguna Mata Niyeu.
correspondence.correspondence: Established at generalized headwater-corridor and junction scale. The selected start extends a short distance southeast of the printed dashed-channel tip within the same upper corridor; an exact spring, headmost channel tip and bank alignment are not assigned. No intervening material connector is missing.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Laguna Mata Niyeu is adjacent to the headward junction area; the selected route is not assigned the lagoon name. No reservoir is depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Cañadón de Yaminué, Rincón de Yaminué and village reach
correspondence.finding: The original map follows the narrow canyon north out of the upland, through Rincón de Yaminué and the Yaminué settlement, then through the northward channel labeled A° Seco Yaminué. Short side ravines and localized vegetated valley-floor features enter the trunk. The regional plan independently identifies Arroyo Yaminué and a historical hydrometric station at El Rincón Yaminué.
correspondence.correspondence: Established through the canyon and settlement corridor. The canyon label and stream label are separately recorded rather than treating every canyon label as a hydronym.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Laguna Blanca and Laguna de Méndez are nearby upland context, not selected lake passages. No impoundment or dam is depicted. Historical map dryness and historical station base flow are not equated with present flow along all reaches.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Yaminué turn through La Angostura and Cabeza de Vaca
correspondence.finding: The selected mapped stream bends east near the La Angostura southern estancia, then proceeds northeast and north past Cabeza de Vaca. The original labels the continuing northern channel A° Yaminué. Tributary ravines join from the surrounding plateau; the larger Treneta valley lies to the southeast and is not renamed Yaminué.
correspondence.correspondence: Established for the north/east bends and continuous channel corridor.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Small wet depressions and valley vegetation occur near the route. No material reservoir or lake crossing interrupts this middle stream.

correspondence.component_scope: RN23 crossing and El Toro wetland-belt connection toward Nahuel Niyeu
correspondence.finding: The Yaminué channel crosses the RN23/rail corridor near La Angostura and Estación Teniente Maza, turns east into the elongated El Toro wetland belt north of the transport corridor, and continues toward the wet hollow at Nahuel Niyeu. The mapped eastward drainage and converging southern channels are visible across this interval; the selected trace is a generalized wetland passage, not a uniformly single open-channel river.
correspondence.correspondence: Established through the wetland/channel complex and the material southern-tributary junction area near Nahuel Niyeu.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Laguna El Toro and its elongated wetland belt are material components. No dam or reservoir is shown.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Arroyo Nahuel Niyeu through Bajo de Valcheta
correspondence.finding: East of the Nahuel Niyeu settlement and its tributary convergence, the original explicitly labels the east/northeast-running drainage A° Nahuel Niyeu. It follows broad wetland tracts through Bajo de Valcheta and past Estancia La Pampa toward the saline-lagoon area. The printed hydronym belongs to this lower receiving drainage and supports the representative candidate.
correspondence.correspondence: Established for the complete lower wetland/channel corridor.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Broad marsh-like/wetland symbols, divided flow traces and small saline depressions characterize the lower route. No reservoir is depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual inland terminal in Laguna Tres Picos
correspondence.finding: The selected lower passage approaches the southern side of the crosshatched saline lagoon labeled Lag. Tres Picos and turns north into that lagoon, where the retained endpoint lies. The original also depicts the neighboring Laguna Indio Muerto to the east and the intervening eastward wetland belt. Tres Picos is the selected terminal waterbody; the broader provincial plan groups Yaminué, Treneta and Comicó under the endorheic Laguna Indio Muerto basin, which is basin context and does not relocate the actual selected endpoint to the neighboring lake.
correspondence.correspondence: Established at saline-lagoon complex scale. No sea outlet, downstream river continuation, exact lake shoreline or permanently wetted condition is asserted.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Natural saline-lagoon/wetland terminal setting, not a reservoir. The river hydronym is not propagated into the lagoon interior.

correspondence.component_scope: actual selected headward approach
correspondence.finding: The selected southwestern beginning lies north of Pocinhos and follows an unnamed small feeder east and southeast into a mapped impounded-water junction. The Peba-labeled approach arrives separately from the southwest. The selected exit continues east/northeast along the Riacho Catolé corridor and then turns north into the receiving drainage directly labeled Rio Curimataú near the northeastern municipal boundary. The initial feeder and impoundment remain unnamed; neither Peba nor Curimataú is assigned uniformly to the opening.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: southern sheet-edge waterbody and upper northward continuation
correspondence.finding: The northern continuation is geographically continuous across the Pocinhos and Solânea originals. It enters and leaves the small mapped waterbody immediately south of Sapo, then runs north/northeast past the Sítio Novo, Jacinto and Poço do Novilho settings toward Passagem. The selected course takes the connected northward trunk rather than the separate Remígio/Covão drainage to the east. The small waterbody name is unestablished.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: upper Curimataú and western tributary distinctions
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues north through the Passagem/Mocó and Barra do Urubu setting, past the separately joining Urubu and Bola-side approaches, then follows the northward-to-eastward bend toward São Lourenço. The map distinguishes the Cantinho, da Cruz and Caraibeira approaches on the west and the northern tributary network. These are separate joining components, not interchangeable headwater names for the selected line.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Cacimba da Várzea reservoir connection
correspondence.finding: After the eastward turn, the selected trunk follows the Cacimba de Dentro–Casserengue boundary corridor into the western arm of the directly labeled Açude Cacimba da Várzea, crosses its connected elongated water body and exits east along the Rio Curimataú. The reservoir name is retained only as a reservoir-component observation. The map also shows numerous separate off-route açudes; their names are not transferred to the selected trunk.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: middle loop toward Caiçara
correspondence.finding: Downstream of the reservoir the selected connected river corridor continues through the Raposa/Umari and Dona Inês–Bananeiras margin, takes its distinctive northward then southward/eastward loop toward Tapera, and joins the Caiçara approach. Solânea depicts the actual blue stream connectors, separate from its highlighted alluvial deposits, and keeps the Salgado, Dantas and other joining approaches distinct. Guarabira directly labels the receiving channel Rio Curimataú at Caiçara and northward beyond it.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Caiçara–Nova Cruz–Pedro Velho receiving trunk
correspondence.finding: The selection follows the named river north beside Caiçara/Logradouro, reaches the Nova Cruz setting and the separate western Calabouço approach, then bends east through the lower valley north of Montanhas toward Pedro Velho. The state original distinguishes this trunk from Pequiri/Piquiri arriving from the northwest and the separate southern Pirari/Espinho-side network. The Canguaretama original supplies the connected lower junction and estuarine approach.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: actual terminal receiving setting
correspondence.finding: The final selected corridor is the lower Curimataú approaching Canguaretama, turning northeast past the separately joining Outeiro toward broad tidal channels and the Barra do Cunhaú coastal outlet. The original map directly labels Rio Curimataú in this estuarine reach and depicts its connected Atlantic opening. The model’s final eastward render extension ends in the coastal setting south of the mapped opening; it is not asserted to trace every tidal branch, the contemporary sandbar passage or an exact surveyed mouth point. The nearby northern Rio Catu outlet and southern Rio Guaju are distinct waters, not alternate names for this selected terminal.
